title: WA UTC Docket 260412 — Order - Open Meeting Final: Order 02 Dismissing Complaint; Authorizing Proposed Tariff Revisions to Become Effective.
summary: Order 02 Dismissing Complaint; Authorizing Proposed Tariff Revisions to Become Effective.
text:
Service Date: July 9, 2026 
BEFORE THE WASHINGTON 
UTILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION 
WASHINGTON UTILITIES AND 
TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION, 
Complainant, 
v. 
EAST SIDE IMPROVEMENT CO., INC, 

Respondent. 
DOCKET UW-260412 
ORDER 02 
DISMISSING COMPLAINT; 
AUTHORIZING PROPOSED TARIFF 
REVISIONS TO BECOME EFFECTIVE 
BACKGROUND 
1 
On May 20, 2026, East Side Improvement Co., Inc. (East Side or Company) filed with 
the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission (Commission) a tariff revision 
that would generate $4,776.82 in additional annual revenue.1 East Side proposes 
implementing a one-time Cost Recovery Surcharge of $106.15 for all customers to 
recover the cost for emergency repairs it performed to repair “two leaks in the irrigation 
system and to replace a valve that was failing in the irrigation pump house.”2 East Side 
provides domestic and irrigation water service to 45 customers on four water systems 
located in Kittitas County. The Company first became regulated by the Commission in 
Docket UW-220369 on July 1, 2022. 
2 
East Side notified its customers by mail dated May 27, 2026, that it is proposing a one-
time surcharge of $106.15 per customer to reimburse the Company for the two leaks it 
repaired to the irrigation system and failing valve it replaced in the irrigation pump 
house. The Company further explains in the customer notice that when the $106.15 
surcharge is combined with the current monthly irrigation rate of $45, it will result in a 
one-time charge of $151.15, to become effective July 1, 2026, if approved by the 
Commission. 

1 The amount sought related to the original repairs was $4,776.82, rather than the $4,766.82 listed 
in Order 01. WUTC v. East Side Improvement Co., Inc., Docket UW-240412, Order 01 at 1 ¶ 1 
(June 29, 2026). 
2 WUTC v. East Side Improvement Co., Inc., Docket UW-240412, Cover Letter from East Side. 

DOCKET UW-260412 
PAGE 2 
ORDER 02 

3 
Commission staff (Staff) reviewed the Company’s filing and determined that the 
Company had not provided sufficient workpapers in support of the surcharge. Staff 
subsequently issued additional data requests to the Company to verify the costs 
associated with the repair. Staff also learned that following the repairs that first caused 
the Company to seek the proposed $4,776.82 surcharge, a pump on the irrigation system 
failed, resulting in $3,179.39 of additional repair expenses and raising the total costs of 
the combined repairs to $7,956.21.3 
4 
This matter was first considered by the Commission at its June 25, 2026, open meeting. 
At that open meeting, the Commission heard from Staff, the Company, the Public 
Counsel Unit of the Washington Attorney General’s Office, and Jon Ward, an East Side 
customer. After considering the information provided in the record and at the open public 
meeting, the Commission suspended the Company’s proposed tariff revisions, 
determining that the Company had not yet demonstrated that the proposed revisions 
would result in rates that are fair, just, reasonable, and sufficient. The Commission 
further required that this matter be set for the July 9, 2026, open meeting, following 
additional Staff review of the Company’s proposed tariff. 
5 
Following the June 25, 2026, open meeting, Staff reviewed all of the information 
provided by the Company concerning the two repairs to its irrigation system. Staff and 
the Company agree that the second set of repairs for $3,179.39 should be included in the 
Company’s proposed surcharge, for a total surcharge amount of $7,956.21. Staff and the 
Company further agree that customers should have the option to either pay a one-time 
surcharge of $176.80 or $29.47 per month over the course of six months. Staff states that 
it is satisfied that the Company has demonstrated the prudence of the costs that its seeks 
to recover via the surcharge and that the Company acknowledges its responsibilities 
regarding the maintenance of its water system and customer notice. 
6 
On July 1, 2026, the Company filed revised tariff pages reflecting its agreement with 
Staff described above. Staff recommends that the Commission allow the Company’s 
tariff revisions, as revised on July 1, 2026, to go into effect as of July 10, 2026, and 
dismiss the complaint in this docket. 
7 
On July 9, 2026, this matter came before the Commission at its regularly scheduled open 
meeting. 

3 WUTC v. East Side Improvement Co., Inc., Docket UW-240412, Order 01 at 2-5 ¶¶ 3-11 (June 
29, 2026) (containing additional factual detail concerning the Company’s repairs). 

DOCKET UW-260412 
PAGE 3 
ORDER 02 

DISCUSSION AND DECISION 
8 
The Commission agrees with Staff’s analysis that the Company has demonstrated that the 
costs of the two sets of repairs to the irrigation portion of the Company’s water system 
were prudent. The Commission also agrees that recovering the costs of both sets of 
repairs through a single surcharge and providing customers with the option to either pay 
the surcharge as a single payment or over the course of six months is reasonable. 
Consequently, the Commission finds that the complaint against the Company in this 
docket should be dismissed, and that the Company’s tariff revisions, as revised on July 1, 
2026, should become effective as of July 10, 2026. Because the Company is funding the 
repairs through a surcharge mechanism, the Company is further responsible for reporting 
within 60 days of the end of each calendar quarter during which the surcharge is in effect: 
(i) beginning balance; (ii) amounts received, detailed by source; (iii) amounts spent, 
detailed by project or expense; (iv) ending balance; and (v) reconciliation of bank balance 
to general ledger.4 
FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS 
9 
(1) 
The Commission is an agency of the state of Washington vested by statute with 
the authority to regulate rates, regulations, and practices of public service 
companies, including water companies. 
10 
(2) 
East Side is a water company and a public service company subject to 
Commission jurisdiction. 
11 
(3) 
This matter came before the Commission at its regularly scheduled meeting on 
July 9, 2026. 
12 
(4) 
Pursuant to RCW 80.04.130(4), the Company bears the burden to demonstrate 
that proposed tariff increases are fair, just, reasonable, and sufficient. 
13 
(5) 
The Company has met its burden to demonstrate that the $7,956.21 it seeks to 
recover through its proposed tariff revisions would result in rates that are fair, 
just, reasonable, and sufficient. 

4 WAC 480-110-455(4)(c). 

DOCKET UW-260412 
PAGE 4 
ORDER 02 

14 
(6) 
Staff has concluded its investigation into whether there is a basis to continue to 
adjudicate this matter and determined that there is no basis for further 
investigation. 
15 
(7) 
The Complaint against the Company should be dismissed. 
16 
(8) 
The Company’s tariff revisions, as revised on July 1, 2026, should become 
effective as of July 10, 2026. 
17 
(9) 
Consistent with WAC 480-110-455(4)(c), the Commission should require the 
Company to file reports to this docket within 60 days of the end of each calendar 
quarter during which the surcharge is in effect containing the information required 
by WAC 480-110-455(4)(c)(i)-(v) pertaining to the approved surcharge 
mechanism. 
ORDER 
THE COMMISSION ORDERS: 
18 
(1) 
The Complaint and Order Suspending Tariff Revisions filed against East Side 
Improvement Co., Inc. is dismissed with prejudice. 
19 
(2) 
The Commission orders the tariff pages filed by East Side Improvement Co., Inc. 
on May 20, 2026, as revised on July 1, 2026, to become effective July 10, 2026. 
20 
(3) 
East Side Improvement Co., Inc. shall file reports to this docket within 60 days of 
the end of each calendar quarter during which the surcharge is in effect containing 
the information required by WAC 480-110-455(4)(c)(i)-(v) pertaining to the 
approved surcharge mechanism. 
21 
(4) 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and East Side 
Improvement Co., Inc. to effectuate the provisions of this Order. 

DOCKET UW-260412 
PAGE 5 
ORDER 02 

DATED at Lacey, Washington, and effective July 9, 2026. 

WASHINGTON UTILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION 
BRIAN J. RYBARIK, Chair
